title: Console UX: Streamlined model version picker + performance profile inspector
creator: Arielle Park
description: Summary: Design and prototype a single-place version selection experience in Redwood Console that makes it simple for customers to pin model versions for routes and to inspect published performance profiles (latency/cost/quality). Goals: 1) Reduce friction for pinning a specific model version during onboarding and rollout; 2) Surface performance profile metadata (throughput, median p95 latency, token cost, model size, quantization notes) so engineers can make an informed choice without leaving the Console; 3) Provide a clear fallback and rollback UX for version rollouts; 4) Track metrics for decisions to feed Optimize recommendations. Target personas: ML engineer configuring a route, product engineer shipping an LLM feature, platform admin reviewing SLAs. Requirements and acceptance criteria: - Main route edit screen includes a compact Version Picker control that shows: current pinned version, available versions with badges (stable, experimental, deprecated), and a quick comparison view when selecting a candidate version. - Comparison view must include side-by-side performance profile entries: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, estimated per-token cost, expected quality delta (from recent evals), KV-cache compatibility, and recommended batch/quantization profile. - UX must allow: pinning single version, pinning a version with a canary percentage (0-20%), and scheduling a rollout window. - When hovering or clicking a profile metric (e.g., p95 latency), an inline tooltip must show the dataset and test conditions used to compute the metric and a link to the full profile page. - Full Performance Profile inspector accessible from the model catalog page; it includes test harness link, last-run date, sample prompts used, and changelog of kernel selections/quantization. - Accessibility: keyboard navigable picker, ARIA labels for comparison fields, color contrast for badges. - Analytics: emit events version_picker.open, version_picker.compare, version_pin.apply, version_rollout.schedule. - No production changes applied until user confirms by saving route; unsaved changes should be persisted temporarily in the Console session. Out of scope: automatic recommendations engine (Optimize) integration and backend API changes are handled in ENG-2272; initial UX will call existing model list and profile endpoints. Mockups and artifacts: - Primary mockups: Figma file (internal): https://redwood.app/figma/console-version-picker-2026 - Prototype (in Figma): https://redwood.app/figma/proto/version-picker - PRD: Confluence doc: https://redwood.app/confluence/display/INF/Console+Version+Pinning+UX - Example API surface used by UX team: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-docs/pull/182 Notes on interactions: 1) Compact state: shows pinned version label and a chevron opens a popover with a searchable list of versions (sorted by stability -> recency -> custom tags). 2) Compare state: selecting two versions launches a split panel; each card fetches the published performance profile and renders sparklines for latency and cost over the last 30 days. 3) Canary flow: slider to select percentage and a schedule picker (cron/simple window). Include a guardrail modal when moving from hosted to dedicated variants if cost delta exceeds a threshold. 4) Rollback flow: from route history allow a single-click revert to previous pinned version with optional release notes. Implementation notes for engineers: - Use existing endpoints from ENG-2272 for profiles; cache profile payloads for 5 minutes client-side. - Provide React component contract: VersionPicker(props: {routeId, currentVersion, onChange}) and PerformanceProfileCard(profileId). - Performance numbers should include test metadata: sequence length distribution, batch size, hardware target used for measurement. Open questions / decisions needed: - Should deprecated versions be hidden by default? (PM leaning: show with a deprecated badge) - What thresholds constitute a cost delta guardrail? (PM to propose numeric thresholds) - Canary telemetry: which logs are required to attribute errors to canary cohort? (Security/Telemetry to advise) QA acceptance items: - Keyboard-only flows for selecting and pinning versions - Tooltip links open in new tabs and go to profile detail view - Canary percentages are honored by backend (ENG verify) - Events captured in analytics pipeline (Product to verify) Rollout plan and staging: - Phase 1 (Beta): internal teams only — enable feature flag console.version_pin_beta - Phase 2: gradual opt-in for orgs with Dedicated plans - Phase 3: GA after two weeks of beta and resolved issues. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: customers mis-pin experimental versions leading to regressions. Mitigation: prominently display stability badges and require a confirmation modal for experimental pins. - Risk: confusion about performance profiles computed under different test conditions. Mitigation: always show test conditions and a link to raw benchmark harness. Timeline and milestones: - Design mockups and prototype complete by 2026-03-05 (done) - Usability testing with 5 engineers by 2026-03-12 (scheduled) - Handoff to ENG + 1-week design QA by 2026-03-20 Stakeholders and reviewers: - PM: Samir Patel - Engineering lead: Nisha Rao - Product Analytics: Jordan Lee - Security/Telemetry reviewer: Mina Okafor
